inputs.original_text: The split comes as some MPs raise the prospect of a new conversation about the party’s leadership Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor has shut down Andrew Hastie’s push for the Liberals to be “open-minded” to increasing taxes on gas companies and winding back concessions for property investors, exposing a clash of philosophies between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. The opposition leader also did not repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump as he refused to say whether or not he endorsed the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: The Liberal Party is fracturing from within as MPs including Andrew Hastie push for higher taxes on gas companies and an end to concessions for property investors. These proposals mark an essential step toward confronting structural inequality by compelling powerful corporations and wealthy property owners to contribute fairly rather than relying on built-in advantages that continue widening gaps for workers and vulnerable communities. Angus Taylor's outright rejection of the ideas exposes the party's deep resistance to reforms that would challenge corporate power or historical privileges, blocking any real progress on labor rights and economic justice. The leader's refusal to echo attacks on Donald Trump and evasion on backing the US and Israel against Iran fit the same pattern of clinging to outdated alliances that divert attention from the urgent domestic institutional changes needed to protect marginalized groups.
